### Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Training margins measure sampled-negative separation and depend on score scale. Training-prefix ranks also measure fit, so neither establishes generalization. (2) Feedback suggests broad associations dilute current-purpose matches. This motivates controlled recency probes without establishing preferences, ownership satisfaction, or compatibility. (3) Actual-model scoring enables architecture-aware interventions. Padding, position IDs, and readout must be checked; unavailable categories and reviews remain unused.

**Related-work insights.** (1) [CETRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.03047) separates recency and relative order, motivating separate interventions without establishing SASRec gains. (2) [Petrov et al.](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) motivate simple history-aware controls: sensitivity alone does not demonstrate useful contextualization. (3) [Krichene–Rendle](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.02263) show sampled-evaluation inconsistencies; auxiliary diagnostics remain distinct from pinned selection. [Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html) additionally motivate caution about repeated validation selection.

Three directions follow: controlled temporal dependence, candidate-dependent ranking robustness, and exploratory diagnostic–validation agreement.

### Framework

| Axis | Existing measurement | Proposed extension | Interpretation limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Representation | Mean embedding cosine | Retain descriptive geometry | Alignment need not imply collapse |
| Ranking | Training margins | Fixed-pool target ranks | Training fit; unobserved items are not dislikes |
| History dependence | None | Paired temporal and position controls | Dependence is not causal preference |
| Selection | Macro validation HR@10 | Preserve unchanged | Auxiliary gains cannot replace it |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Paired temporal diagnostic adapter — 5/7/5.** Originality: useful controlled combination (+), established perturbations (−). Potential: reusable across architectures (+), generalization remains unproven (−). Difficulty: existing hooks suffice for basic probes (+), masking, readout, and position controls require care (−).
2. **Candidate-stress diagnostic panel — 4/7/5.** Originality: combines candidate regimes (+), standard components (−). Potential: reveals pool sensitivity (+), benchmark agreement unknown (−). Difficulty: TF-IDF needs no pretrained weights (+), catalog scoring consumes budget (−).
3. **Learned recent-history residual scorer — 4/7/6.** Originality: tests the feedback hypothesis (+), familiar recency mixtures (−). Potential: may improve immediate relevance (+), may suppress recurring interests (−). Difficulty: small scoring addition (+), retraining and predictor synchronization cost budget (−).

### Selected idea: paired temporal diagnostic adapter

At 0% progress, prioritize trustworthy measurement before architecture changes. Sample targets from training histories and use strictly preceding prefixes; label results as training-fit diagnostics. Keep earlier repeated target occurrences. Freeze candidate IDs, eligibility, perturbation strengths, repeats, and seeds across comparisons and models.

Compare equal-count recent, older, and random removal; separately shuffle earlier interactions while fixing the latest. Distinguish hole masking, packing with preserved position IDs, and ordinary reindexed packing. Test final-item removal separately. Fixed-position real-item substitutions provide a complementary content probe. Verify padding exclusion, finite outputs, and consistent readout before interpretation; unsupported controls must be reported unavailable.

Report paired ranks, top-10 overlap, sample counts, and category-macro intervals. Average repeats within users, then bootstrap paired users within category. Retain simple last-item, transition, and pooling controls as descriptive comparators. Predeclare exploratory checkpoint correlations and improvement-direction agreement with unchanged host HR@10; log every trial. Intervals exclude training-seed and selection uncertainty. Preserve required interfaces, restore model mode, bound scoring costs, and retain full-catalog unseen recommendations for all twenty simulator users.

idea.description: Implement a paired temporal diagnostic adapter that measures dependence on recent content, earlier order, and positional handling through the actual trained model, with explicit controls for padding artifacts and training memorization.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests broad associations sometimes outrank specific recent interests, while existing embedding and margin probes cannot distinguish content, order, recency, or implementation effects. At 0% progress, controlled measurements are a feasible foundation before training a recency residual scorer. Training-history diagnostics establish model dependence and fit; only unchanged host validation measures benchmark generalization, and repeated validation consultation remains exploratory.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use view.model as the actual nn.Module; enter eval mode under torch.inference_mode() and restore its previous training state in finally. Retain existing embedding and margin probes, but explicitly define mean cosine as directional alignment rather than proof of collapse. Category breakdowns must remain empty because category metadata is unavailable; do not use reviews, ratings, prices, stores, or simulator traits.

Use log2feats and predict_score through an architecture-specific scoring adapter. Document left/right padding, positional indexing, attention masks, and readout. Baseline SASRec scores the final array position; choosing the last nonzero ID automatically is not a generally valid replacement. Causal masks do not exclude padded keys, and key padding masks do not zero padded query outputs. Verify the actual implementation rather than assuming padding embedding zero makes holes inert. Do not silently change trained inference behavior to repair a diagnostic. Any correction that changes the trained model requires a separate training change and synchronized predictor writer.

A concrete bounded default is up to 50 eligible training users per dataset, sampled with a local seed-42 generator and sorted ID ordering. For each user select the final training event as target and use its preceding prefix, truncated to the model context length. Require at least five prefix events for matched removal controls and report excluded-user counts. These targets participated in optimization and therefore measure training fit. Never read validation or test labels through the probe. Earlier occurrences of the target remain in the prefix. Do not modify preprocessing or split membership.

For sampled diagnostics use the target once plus 99 unique uniform negatives, excluding padding, target, and original-prefix IDs; reuse the exact pool under every intervention. If fewer than 99 eligible negatives exist, report the example unavailable rather than sampling duplicates. A separate complete-training-history exclusion condition may be reported, keeping the target eligible even if repeated. Persist pools and exclusion-policy identifiers beneath the trial directory. These auxiliary pools are not substitutes for the host's pinned validation candidates. Use descending score then ascending item ID for diagnostic ties; preserve host tie handling for official metrics.

Set removal count m=max(1,floor(0.2*(n-1))) among the n-1 prefix events preceding the final event. Compare the m most recent eligible events, m oldest events, and m uniformly sampled eligible events while retaining the final event. Use three deterministic repeats for random removal and shuffling; fixed interventions need one evaluation. Compare earlier-only shuffling with full shuffling. Test deletion of the final event separately and repack to the ordinary final query position. Log selected indices and effective intervention strength for reproduction.

For removal controls distinguish holes, packing with original position IDs retained, and ordinary reindexed packing. With correctly excluded padded keys, identical surviving position IDs, order, and readout, holes and preserved-position packing should closely agree within documented numerical tolerance. Check finite outputs and perturb padded-key representations to verify exclusion. If the architecture cannot expose position IDs or masks without changing its semantics, report that control unsupported; do not claim recency identification from unverified hole masking. Complement removal with fixed-position substitutions using actual same-dataset items: sample unseen donor items from the same training-frequency decile, using deterministic nearest-decile fallback. These substitutions avoid holes but remain potentially out of distribution and are not preference counterfactuals.

Report original and perturbed target ranks, reciprocal ranks, sampled HR@10, rank differences, top-10 overlap defined as intersection size divided by ten, sample counts, and explicit metric definitions. Keep sampled overlap distinct from full-catalog overlap. Average repeats within user; bootstrap users independently within each dataset using 1,000 seed-42 replicates while carrying all paired outcomes together. Compute each replicate's equally weighted four-dataset macro difference and percentile 95% interval. If any category has no eligible examples, report the four-category macro statistic unavailable rather than silently averaging fewer categories. Intervals condition on fixed trained models and candidate pools; they exclude training-seed uncertainty and repeated-selection bias.

Include inexpensive descriptive controls: last-item dot-product scoring using learned item embeddings; a transition baseline fitted only from adjacent training interactions with add-one smoothing and frequency-weighted aggregation over the prefix; and mean normalized history-embedding similarity. These controls identify plausible shortcuts but are themselves fitted on training data and are not proof of useful generalization. Stratify descriptively by history length and repeated-item fraction; do not equate repeated IDs with semantic purpose.

Before further comparisons, freeze diagnostic definitions and the checkpoint schedule. Across all logged checkpoints and trials, report exploratory Spearman correlation between predeclared diagnostic quantities and official macro validation HR@10, adjacent-checkpoint improvement-direction agreement with ties reported separately, and category consistency. Correlated checkpoints are not independent replications; missing outcomes remain missing. If the host does not expose paired per-user validation outcomes, report only its available aggregate results and omit validation bootstrap intervals. Never reconstruct or alter the evaluator. Winner intervals do not correct repeated-selection optimism; independent confirmation awaits the host's final evaluation.

For the twenty required simulator users, preserve five users per dataset and full-catalog unseen-item scoring. Encode each history once per perturbation, score catalog chunks, mask padding and complete training histories, and merge chunk-local top-k results with deterministic tie handling. Cache item representations only while weights remain fixed; key all caches by checkpoint, dataset, history, perturbation, and exclusion policy. Preallocate at most 600 GPU-seconds for this initial diagnostic phase within the shared 43,200-second budget, reserving required simulator scoring before optional controls. Log elapsed time and omissions; do not replace required full-catalog recommendations with sampled candidates.

Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four dataset routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, and the existing SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Write all artifacts beneath the trial directory. No extra datasets or pretrained weights are required. Subsequent architecture changes must update training and the predictor writer together.

originality.positive: Combines matched temporal interventions, position and padding checks, fixed candidate eligibility, and architecture-aware scoring within the required adapter.
originality.negative: The component techniques are established; the contribution is a careful diagnostic protocol rather than a new recommendation model.

future_potential.positive: Provides reusable evidence for deciding whether recency mechanisms or simpler history-aware scorers deserve training budget.
future_potential.negative: Training memorization, out-of-distribution interventions, and repeated validation selection limit claims that diagnostic improvements predict generalization.

code_difficulty.positive: Basic paired scoring reuses existing hooks and needs no retraining, external data, or pretrained weights.
code_difficulty.negative: Position-preserving controls, padding verification, deterministic catalog top-k, cache correctness, and paired uncertainty require more work than the original difficulty rating acknowledged.

related_work.title: CETRec (2025)
contributions: Separates absolute recency from relative interaction order in LLM recommendation, motivating distinct intervention controls.
limitations: Its architectural findings do not establish benefits for SASRec on these Amazon datasets.

related_work.title: Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling?
contributions: Reports strong history-aware pairwise transition controls, motivating tests of whether complex sequence dependence improves accuracy.
limitations: The supplied results concern different datasets and cannot predict performance on the four requested categories.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking evaluation can disagree with full-catalog model comparisons.
limitations: Does not identify which auxiliary diagnostic will predict this benchmark's fixed sampled HR@10.

related_work.title: PyTorch MultiheadAttention documentation
contributions: Documents separate attention and key-padding masks, supporting explicit checks of padded-key exclusion.
limitations: API behavior alone does not establish how the actual trained model handles padding, positions, or query readout.

related_work.title: Original SASRec implementation
contributions: Provides reference implementations of positional embeddings, masking, intermediate padded-state handling, and final-position prediction.
limitations: The trial's implementation may differ; diagnostic behavior must be checked against the actual trained module.

related_work.title: SASRec PyTorch implementation by pmixer
contributions: Illustrates implementation-specific causal masking and final-array-position scoring.
limitations: Repository code can change, and its behavior cannot be assumed to match the pinned RecHarness baseline.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how optimizing model selection against finite evaluation data can produce selection bias.
limitations: Does not provide a correction for this adaptive search under fixed splits; logging and conditional intervals do not remove selection optimism.

related_work.title: RecBole trainer implementation
contributions: Documents split prediction and history masking relevant to bounded-memory full-catalog recommendation.
limitations: Serves as an implementation reference, not evidence that auxiliary full-catalog diagnostics predict the host's sampled benchmark.
